Subject: Unexpected p99 spikes on extended-history requests

Hi Ava / Lauren,

We're seeing an abrupt spike in p95/p99 latency starting yesterday evening for requests that include long history (we use ~16k-32k token windows for multi-turn summaries). Key observations from our side: 
- p95 for the hosted API requests rose from ~420ms -> ~1.3s; p99 spiked to ~2.1s for a segment of traffic between 22:30-23:20 PST 5/20.
- Error rate increased (502/504) on ~4% of long-history calls during the window; short-context calls (<=2k) unaffected.
- Throughput dropped on some tenants due to retry storms.

Attached is a small log snippet and a basic trace sample (request_log_snippet.txt). We're a bit concerned because this pattern has re-occurred over the last 36 hours and is starting to affect our customer SLAs. Can your team confirm whether anything changed on the hosted side (model variant rollouts, kernel updates, autoscaler policy) or if this is a workload-related degradation?

We can make a recording of a failing session if helpful. Appreciate fast triage — this impacts our production workflows.

Thanks,
Samir Desai
Senior Engineering Manager
BrightBridge Health

Subject: RE: Unexpected p99 spikes on extended-history requests — mitigation & findings

Samir — thanks for your patience. Ops has completed a short investigation and we've applied a set of mitigations; summary below with next steps.

What we found (ops summary):
- No rollout of new primary model during the 5/20 window. There was a kernel-level dispatch change (small optimization) pushed to canary nodes on 5/19 that affected how KV cache is sharded across accelerator memory for long-kv contexts. Canary sampling was limited but correlated with the earliest anomalies.
- The issue surfaced primarily on 16k-32k requests where KV cache miss amplification and occasional memory compaction caused tail pauses at p99.

Actions taken (applied 5/24):
- Immediate: routed BrightBridge long-history production traffic to a stable model-variant path that uses the previous KV-sharding behavior. This reduced p99 from ~2.1s -> ~480ms in our test window.
- Autoscaler: temporarily increased burst capacity for the affected pool to reduce queuing while we observe steady-state.
- Rate-limiting: applied soft per-tenant long-window throttles to dampen retry amplification for 24-48 hours.
- Observability: uploaded full traces to the shared Drive link and created JIRA INF-9123 to track the postmortem and code fix. Trace artifact: perf_traces_20270521.zip (attached).

Recommended next steps (timeline):
- Short (48-72h): monitor p99/p95 and error rates. If stable, remove soft throttles.
- Mid (2 weeks): ship a guarded rollback/hotfix to canary kernel dispatch to restore previous KV sharding logic with improved test coverage for long-window paths.
- Long (1-2 months): invest in adaptive KV eviction and prefix-caching for heavy long-history tenants; update our continuous batching policies to detect long-window bursts and route preemptively.

Compensation: Vivek — please advise exec on SLA credit guidance. From ops perspective, we'll bundle a 10% credit for the affected billing window as a baseline if the customer requests it; we can adjust based on final impact analysis.

Attachments: perf_traces_20270521.zip, mitigation_playbook_v1.md

Samir — apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as high priority and will provide a daily update until metrics are stable. Can we schedule a 30-min technical sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT to walk traces and validate the fix?

Regards,
